And I saw that valley, in which there was a great disturbance and a churning of the waters.

And when all this happened, from those drops of fire and the disturbance that shook them in that place, a smell of sulfur arose and mingled with those waters. And that valley of the angels who led others astray burns beneath that land.
From its valleys flow rivers of fire, where those angels who led the inhabitants of the earth astray will be punished.

In those days, those waters will serve the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and the inhabitants of the earth for the healing of soul and body, but for the punishment of the spirit. Their spirits will be filled with lust, so that they will be punished in their bodies, because they denied the Lord of Spirits. They see their punishment every day, yet do not believe in his name.
As their bodies burn intensely, so their spirits will undergo a change forever and ever, because there is no one before the Lord of Spirits who will speak on behalf of their weeping.
For punishment will come upon them, because they believe in the lust of their bodies and deny the spirit of the Lord.

Those waters will undergo a change at that time. When those angels are punished in those days, the appearance of those springs of water will change. When the angels ascend, that water of the springs will change and grow cold.
And I heard holy Michael speak and say, “This punishment by which the angels are punished is a testimony to the kings, the powerful, and those who possess the earth.

For these waters of punishment serve to heal the bodies of the angels and to bring death to their bodies. Yet they do not see or believe that those waters will change and become a fire that burns forever.”

After this, he gave me knowledge of all the mysteries in a book from my grandfather Enoch, and of the parables that had been given to him. He brought them together for me in the account of the Book of Parables.

On that day holy Michael spoke to Raphael, saying, “The power of the spirit carries me away and makes me tremble. As for the severity of the punishment of the secret angels, who can endure the severity of the punishment that has been carried out and remains, before which they melt away?”

Again holy Michael spoke to Raphael and said, “Whose heart would not soften over it, and whose inward parts would not be troubled by this sentence of punishment that has gone out against them, because of those among them who brought them out in this way?”

When he stood before the Lord of Spirits, holy Michael said this to Raphael: “There will be no mercy for them in the Lord’s sight, because the Lord of Spirits is angry with them, because they act as though they were the Lord.
For this reason the hidden punishment will come upon them forever and ever. Neither angel nor human will receive a share in it; they alone will receive their punishment forever and ever.”
And after this, judgment will terrify them and make them tremble, because they showed this to those who dwell on dry land.

And here are the names of those angels; these are their names: the first of them, Semyaza; the second, Arstiqifa; the third, Armen; the fourth, Kokabiel; the fifth, Turiel; the sixth, Rumyal; the seventh, Daniel; the eighth, Nuqael; the ninth, Baraqiel; the tenth, Azazel; the eleventh, Armaros; the twelfth, Bataryal; the thirteenth, Basasael; the fourteenth, Ananel; the fifteenth, Turyal; the sixteenth, Simasipiel; the seventeenth, Yetariel; the eighteenth, Tumael; the nineteenth, Tarel; the twentieth, Rumael; the twenty-first, Azazel.
These are the chiefs of their angels and their names: their commanders of hundreds, their commanders of fifties, and their commanders of tens.
The name of the first is Jeqon. He is the one who led all the sons of the angels astray, brought them down onto the earth, and led them astray through the daughters of humankind.
The name of the second is Asbeel. He taught evil counsel to the sons of the holy angels and led them astray so that they corrupted their bodies with the daughters of humankind.

And the third was named Gadreel. He was the one who showed deadly blows to human beings. He led Eve astray, and he showed human beings the instruments of death: the shield, armor, the sword for killing, and all the instruments of death.
And from his hand they went out against those who dwell on dry land, from that time and forever.
The name of the fourth is Penemue. He showed the children of humankind the bitter and the sweet, and showed them all the secrets of their wisdom.
He taught people writing with ink and paper. Because of this, many have gone astray from age to age, down to this very day.
For human beings were not born for such a purpose: to establish their faith with pen and ink.

For human beings were created only to be like the angels, to remain righteous and pure. Death, which destroys everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge of theirs they perish, and because of this, power devours me.

The name of the fifth is Kasdeja. He showed the children of humankind all the evil blows of spirits and demons, the blows against the embryo in the womb so that it is miscarried, the blows against the soul through the serpent’s bite, and the blows that occur at midday through the offspring of the serpent whose name is Tabaet.
This is the account of Kasbeel, the chief of the oath, who revealed it to the holy ones when the Most High dwelt in glory; its name is Biqa.

He told holy Michael to show them his secret name, so that they could see that secret name and invoke it in an oath, so that those who revealed everything hidden to the children of humankind would tremble before that name and oath.
This is the power of this oath, for it is mighty and strong. He placed that oath, Akae, in the hand of holy Michael.
These are the mysteries of this oath, and they were made firm by his oath. Heaven was suspended before the world was created, and remains so forever.
By it the earth was established upon the water, and from the hidden places of the mountains pleasant waters come for living creatures, from the creation of the world and forever.
By that oath the sea was created, and he placed sand as its foundation for the time of wrath, so that it would not cross its boundary, from the creation of the world and forever.
By that oath the depths are firmly established and stand still, and they do not move from their places, from eternity and forever.
By that oath the sun and moon complete their courses and do not transgress the command given to them, from eternity and forever.
By that oath the stars complete their courses. He calls their names, and they answer him, from eternity and forever.
Likewise, the spirits of the waters, the spirits of the winds, and all their spirits and their paths, from every company of spirits.

There the storehouses of the thunder’s voice and the lightning’s brightness are guarded. There the storehouses of hail and ice are guarded, along with the storehouses of mist and the storehouses of rain and dew.

All these profess faith and give thanks before the Lord of Spirits, and they praise him with all their strength. Their nourishment consists entirely of thanksgiving, and they give thanks, praise, and exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
This oath is firmly established over them, and they are preserved by it. Their paths are preserved, and their courses do not fall into ruin.
They had great joy, and they blessed, praised, and exalted because the name of the Son of Man had been revealed to them.
And he sat on the throne of his glory, and all judgment was entrusted to him, the Son of Man. He will remove and destroy sinners from the face of the earth, and those who led the world astray.
They will be bound with chains and shut up in their gathering place of destruction, and all their deeds will pass away from the face of the earth.

From now on there will be nothing corruptible, because the Son of Man has appeared and seated himself upon the throne of his glory. All evil will pass away and depart from before his face, and they will speak to that Son of Man, and he will stand firm before the Lord of Spirits. This is the third parable of Enoch.
After this, his name, while he was alive, was raised up to that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits, from among those who dwell on dry land.
He was raised up in the chariots of the spirit, and his name departed from among them.

From that day I was no longer counted among them. He placed me between the two winds, between the north and the west, where the angels took cords to measure out for me the place for the chosen and the righteous.
There I saw the ancient fathers and the righteous who have dwelt in that place from ancient times.

After this, my spirit was carried away and ascended into the heaven of heavens. I saw the sons of the holy angels walking upon flames of fire. Their clothes were white, as were their robes, and the brightness of their faces was like snow.
I saw two rivers of fire, and the brightness of that fire shone like jacinth. And [?] fell on my face before the Lord of Spirits.
Michael the angel, one of the archangels, took me by my right hand, raised me up, and brought me out to all the hidden things of mercy and the hidden things of righteousness.
He showed me all the hidden things of the ends of heaven and all the storehouses of the stars and lights, from which they all come out before the holy ones.
The spirit carried Enoch away into the heaven of heavens. There, in the midst of that light, I saw something built of stones of ice, and among those stones were tongues of living fire.
My spirit saw the ring surrounding that house of fire. On its four sides were streams full of living fire, and they surrounded that house.
Around it were cherubim, seraphim, and ophanim. These are the ones who do not sleep and who guard the throne of his glory.

I saw angels beyond counting, myriads upon myriads and tens of thousands upon tens of thousands, surrounding that house. Michael, Gabriel, Phanuel, Raphael, and the holy angels who are above the heavens entered and left that house.
And Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Phanuel came out of that house, along with countless holy angels.
With them was the Head of Days. His head was like white, pure wool, and his clothing was indescribable.
And I fell on my face, and all my flesh melted, and my spirit was transformed. I cried out with a loud voice, with a powerful spirit, and blessed and praised and exalted.
And these blessings that came from my mouth were pleasing before that Head of Days.
And that Head of Days came with Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Phanuel, and thousands and tens of thousands of thousands of angels beyond counting.

And that angel came to me and greeted me with his voice and said to me, “You are the Son of Man who was born for righteousness. Righteousness has settled upon you, and the righteousness of the Head of Days will not abandon you.”

And he said to me, “He will proclaim peace to you in his name for all eternity to come, because peace has gone out from there since the creation of the world. And so it will be for you forever and ever.

And all will live and walk on your path, while righteousness will never abandon you. Their dwelling will be with you, and their portion will be with you, and they will not be separated from you forever and ever.”
And so there will be length of days with that Son of Man, and there will be peace for the righteous. His path will be straight for the righteous, in the name of the Lord of Spirits, forever.

The book of the movements of the lights of heaven, each according to its group, each according to its authority and its season, each according to its name, its origin, and its month, which Uriel, the holy angel who was with me and who is their guide, showed me; and their entire account, as he showed it to me, for all the years of the world and forever, until a new work is made that will last forever.
And this is the first rule of the lights: the sun, a light, rises through the gates of heaven toward the east, and sets through the gates of heaven in the west.

And I saw six gates through which the sun rises and six gates where the sun sets. The moon rises and sets through those gates, and the leaders of the stars of heaven, together with those they lead: six in the east and six in the west. All of them are aligned, one after another, and there are many windows to the right and left of that gate.
And first the greater light comes out, whose name is the sun. Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and it is entirely filled with fire that gives light and heat.
And the wind drives the chariot in which it rises. The sun sets from heaven and returns through the north to go to the east, and it is guided to enter that gate and shine across the face of heaven.
And in this way it rises in the first month through the great gate. It comes out through the fourth of those six gates toward the east.
And in that fourth gate, through which the sun rises in the first month, there are twelve open gates from which flames come out when they are opened at their appointed times.
When the sun rises in heaven, it comes out through that fourth gate for thirty mornings, and descends directly through the fourth gate in the west of heaven.
And during those days, the day grows longer day by day, and the night grows shorter night by night, until thirty mornings have passed.
And on that day, the day is two parts longer than the night. The day amounts to exactly ten parts, and the night amounts to eight parts.
And the sun rises through that fourth gate and sets through the fourth gate. It returns to the fifth gate in the east for thirty mornings, rising through it and setting through the fifth gate.
And then the day grows longer by two parts, and the day amounts to eleven parts. The night grows shorter and amounts to seven parts.
And the sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate. It rises and sets through the sixth gate for thirty-one mornings, in accordance with its sign.
And on that day, daylight becomes longer than night, and daylight becomes twice as long as night. Daylight becomes twelve parts, and night becomes shorter and amounts to six parts.
And the sun rises so that the day becomes shorter and the night becomes longer. The sun returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and rises through it and sets for thirty mornings.
And when thirty mornings have been completed, daylight decreases by exactly one part. Daylight becomes eleven parts, and night seven parts.
And the sun leaves the west through that sixth gate and travels east. It rises through the fifth gate for thirty mornings and sets in the west again through the fifth western gate.
And on that day, daylight decreases by two parts. Daylight becomes ten parts, and night eight parts.
And the sun rises through that fifth gate and sets through the fifth gate in the west. It rises through the fourth gate, in accordance with its sign, for thirty-one mornings, and sets in the west.
And on that day, the day becomes equal to the night, and they are equal. The night amounts to nine parts, and the day to nine parts.
And the sun rises through that gate and sets in the west. It returns to the east and rises through the third gate for thirty mornings, and sets in the west through the third gate.
And on that day, the night grows longer night by night for thirty mornings, and the day grows shorter day by day for thirty days. The night amounts to exactly ten parts, and the day to eight parts.

And the sun rises through that third gate and sets through the third gate in the evening. It returns to the east, and the sun rises through the second gate in the east for thirty mornings. In the same way, it sets through the second gate in the west of heaven.
And on that day, night becomes eleven parts, and daylight seven parts.

On that day the sun comes out through that second gate and sets in the west through the second gate. It returns to the east and comes out through the first gate for thirty-one mornings, according to my sign, and sets in the west through the first gate.
On that day the night grows longer and becomes twice as long as the day. The night is exactly twelve parts, and the day seven parts.
The sun has completed its turning points and again circles over these turning points. It enters through that gate for thirty mornings, and in the west it sets opposite it.
On that day it decreases from its length by one measure, that is, one part. The night is eleven parts, and the day one part.
The sun returns and enters the second gate in the east. It returns to that turning point for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
On that day the night decreases from its length. The night is ten parts, and the day eight parts.

And on that day, the sun comes out through that second gate and sets in the west. It returns east and rises through the third gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign, and sets in the west of heaven.
On that day the night grows shorter and becomes nine parts, and the day becomes nine parts. The night is equal to the day, and the year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.
The lengthening of the day and night and the shortening of the day and night are determined by the sun's course.
Because of it, its course grows longer, and the day grows shorter day by day, and the night grows shorter night by night.
This is the law of the sun, its course and its return. When it returns, it returns and comes out for sixty days. This is the great light of the world, which is called the sun forever and ever.
This is the great light that comes out, which is named according to its appearance, as the Lord commanded.

In this way it comes out and enters. It does not diminish or rest, but runs day and night in its chariot. Its light shines seven times more brightly than the moon's, but the sizes of the two are equal.
After this law, I saw another law for the small light whose name is the moon.
Its circumference is like the circumference of heaven. The wind blows the chariot on which it rides, and light is given to it in a measured amount.
Each month its rising and setting change, and its days are like the days of the sun. When its light becomes full, its light is one-seventh of the sun's light.

This is how it rises. Its beginning toward the east comes out on the thirtieth morning [?]. On that day it becomes visible and becomes the beginning of the month for you, for thirty mornings, together with the sun, through the gate from which the sun comes out.
Half of it is distant by one of seven parts, and its whole circumference is empty, without light except for a seventh part of it out of the fourteen parts of its light.
On the day when it receives a seventh part of half its light, it becomes one and a half parts out of seven [?].

It sets with the sun, and when the sun rises, the moon rises with it and receives half a part of light. On that night, at the beginning of its morning, before the moon's day, the moon sets with the sun, and on that night thirteen and a half parts of it are dark.
On that day it rises with exactly a seventh part. It comes out and moves away from the rising of the sun, and during the remainder of its day it shines with fourteen parts.
I saw another course and law for it, according to which it follows its monthly course.

Uriel, the holy angel who guides them all, showed me everything. I wrote down their positions as he showed me, and I wrote down their months as they are, and the appearance of their light until fifteen days were completed.
In fourteen parts it completes all its light in the east, and in fourteen parts it completes all its darkness in the west.
In certain months it completes its settings, and in certain months it follows its courses one by one.
In two months it sets with the sun through these two gates in the middle, through the third and fourth gates.

It rises for seven days, makes its circuit, and returns again through the gate through which the sun rises. There it completes all its light, and it draws away from the sun. For eight days it enters through the sixth gate, from which the sun rises.

When the sun comes out through the fourth gate, it comes out for seven days until it comes out through the fifth. Then it returns for seven days through the fourth gate, completes all its light, turns aside, and enters through the first gate for eight days.
Then it returns for seven days through the fourth gate, through which the sun comes out.
In this way I saw their positions, according to the arrangement of their months, as the sun rises and sets.
And during those days of five years, thirty days accrue to the sun. All the days that accrue to one year out of those five years, when complete, amount to three hundred and sixty-four days.
Their advance upon the sun and the stars amounts to six days in five years; at six days each, it amounts to thirty days. The moon falls thirty days behind the sun and the stars.

And the moon brings the years exactly into order. All of them, according to their positions, are neither a day early nor a day late, but they change the year with exact accuracy, each consisting of three hundred and sixty-four days.

For three years, its days are one thousand and ninety-two; and for five years, its days are one thousand eight hundred and twenty, so that for eight years there are two thousand nine hundred and twelve days.
For the moon alone, its days in three years amount to one thousand and sixty-two days. In five years it falls fifty days short, because at its rising it increases by sixty-two days.
In five years there are one thousand seven hundred and seventy days, so that the moon's days in eight years amount to two thousand eight hundred and thirty-two days.
For its shortfall in eight years is eighty days, and all the days by which it falls short in eight years are eighty.
The year is completed accurately according to their positions and the position of the sun, which rise through the gates through which it rises and sets for thirty days.

Their leaders, the chiefs of thousands who are over all creation and over all the stars, together with the four that are added, do not depart from their positions, in accordance with the entire reckoning of the year. These serve on the four days that are not counted in the reckoning of the year.

Because of them, people make errors concerning them, for these lights serve faithfully in the positions of the world: one in the first gate, one in the third gate, one in the fourth gate, and one in the sixth gate. The exact ordering of the world is completed in three hundred and sixty-four positions of the world.

For Uriel showed me the signs, seasons, years, and days—the angel whom the Lord of eternal glory placed over all the lights of heaven and in the world, so that they might rule across the face of heaven, appear above the earth, and lead the day and the night: the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the serving bodies that make their circuits in all the chariots of heaven.

In this way Uriel showed me twelve open gates, open around the circuit of the sun's chariot in heaven. Through them the sun's feet come out, and through them heat comes out upon the earth when they are opened at their appointed seasons.
And there are openings for the winds and for the spirit of the dew, when they are opened in their seasons in heaven at its extremities.
I saw twelve gates in heaven at the ends of the earth, through which the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the works of heaven come out, in the east and in the west.

There are many open windows to their right and to their left. One window, in its season, gives off heat, like these gates through which the stars come out as he commanded them, and through which they set according to their number.
I saw chariots in heaven running through the world above and below these gates, through which the stars that do not set turn back.
One is greater than all of them, and it circles the whole world.
At the ends of the earth I saw twelve open gates for all the winds, through which the winds come out and blow upon the earth.
Three of them are open at the front of heaven, three in the west, three on the right side of heaven, and three on the left.
The first three face east, three face north, three behind them are on the left toward the south, and three are in the west.

From four of them come winds of blessing and peace, and from those eight come winds of punishment. When they are sent out, they destroy the whole earth, the water upon it, all who dwell upon it, and everything that is in the water and on dry land.
The first wind comes out through these gates, and its name is the east wind. Through the first gate, which faces east and inclines toward the south, come destruction, dryness, heat, and devastation.
Through the second gate, the middle one, it comes out straight, and through it come rain, fruitfulness, peace, and dew. Through the third gate, which faces north, come cold and dryness.
After these, the winds toward the south come out through the first three gates. Through the first of these gates, which inclines toward the east, comes a hot wind.
Through the gate next to it, the middle one, come a pleasant fragrance, dew, rain, peace, and life.
Through the third gate, which faces west, come dew, rain, locusts, and destruction.

And after these come the winds toward the north, which is called the sea. From the seventh gate, one of the three, which faces east and inclines toward the south, come dew, rain, locusts, and destruction.

And from the middle gate, which faces straight ahead, come rain, dew, life, and peace. And from the third gate, which faces west and inclines toward the north, come mist, hoarfrost, snow, rain, dew, and locusts.
And after these come the four winds toward the west. From the first gate, which inclines toward the north, come dew, rain, hoarfrost, cold, snow, and frost.
And from the middle gate come dew, rain, peace, and blessing. And from the last gate, which faces south, come drought, destruction, heat, and ruin.
And the twelve gates of the four gates of heaven are complete. I have shown you all their commands, all their plagues, and all their peace, my son Methuselah.

They call the first wind the morning wind, because it is the first. And they call the second the south, because the Most High descends there, and especially there descends the one who is blessed forever.
And the wind from the west is called Diminished, because there all the lights of heaven diminish and descend.

And the fourth wind, which is called the north, is divided into three parts. One of them is a dwelling place for people; another contains seas of water, abysses, forests, rivers, darkness, and mist; and the third part contains the garden of righteousness.
And I saw seven tall mountains, taller than all the mountains on earth. From them comes hoarfrost, and days, seasons, and years pass and go by.
And I saw seven rivers on the earth, larger than all the other rivers. One of them comes from the west and pours its water into the great sea.
And these two come from the north as far as the sea, and pour their water into the Red Sea in the east.
And the remaining four flow out on the northern side as far as their sea, the Red Sea. And two empty into the great sea, and there, they say, is the desert.
I saw seven large islands in the sea and on the land: two on the land and five in the great sea.
The names of the sun are these: one is Orjares, and the other is Tomas.
And the moon has four names. Its first name is Asonja, its second Ebla, its third Benase, and its fourth Erae.
These are the two great lights. Their circles are like the circle of heaven, and the sizes of the two are equal.
In the sun’s disk there are seven portions of light in excess of the moon’s. It is imparted in measured amounts until the seventh portion of the sun has passed.
And they set and enter the gates of the west, go around by way of the north, and come out through the gates of the east over the face of heaven.
And when the moon rises, it appears in heaven, and it has half of a seventh part of light. On the fourteenth day it completes all its light.

And three times five parts of light are placed in it, until its light is complete on the fifteenth day, as a sign of the year. It amounts to three times five parts, and the moon becomes full by half of a seventh part.

And in its waning, on the first day its light decreases to fourteen parts; on the second it decreases to thirteen parts; on the third it decreases to twelve parts; on the fourth it decreases to eleven parts; on the fifth it decreases to ten parts; on the sixth it decreases to nine parts; on the seventh it decreases to eight parts; on the eighth it decreases to seven parts; on the ninth it decreases to six parts; on the tenth it decreases to five parts; on the eleventh it decreases to four parts; on the twelfth it decreases to three parts; on the thirteenth it decreases to two parts; and on the fourteenth it decreases to half of a seventh part. On the fifteenth day, all the light remaining from the whole is exhausted.
And in certain months the moon has twenty-nine days, and sometimes twenty-eight.
And the angel Uriel showed me another order: when light is placed in the moon, and from where it is placed in it from the sun.
Throughout the time that the moon travels, it places its light before the sun, and by fifteen days its light is complete in heaven. And when it [?] completely, its light is complete in heaven.
And the first day is called the new moon, because on that day light rises upon it.

And it becomes completely full on the day when the sun descends into the west. It rises from the east at night, and the moon shines throughout the night until the sun rises before it, and the moon appears before the sun.
And from the place where the moon’s light comes out, it decreases again until all its light is gone and the days of the month have passed, and its disk remains bare, without light.

For three months it makes thirty days in its period, and for three months it makes twenty-nine days each. During these it undergoes its decrease in the first period and at the first gate, over one hundred and seventy-seven days.
And during the period of its rising, it appears for thirty days each in three months, and for twenty-nine days each in three months.
At night it appears in groups of twenty [?], like a man, and by day like the sky, for it has nothing else except its own light.
And now, my son Methuselah, I have shown you everything, and the entire order of the stars of heaven is complete.
And he showed me their entire order for every day and every season, for every dominion and every year, for its rising and its appointed command, and for every month and every week.
And the decrease of the moon takes place at the sixth gate, for at this sixth gate its light becomes full, and from there comes the beginning of the month and its decrease.
This takes place at the first gate in its period, until one hundred and seventy-seven days have been completed, amounting to twenty-five weeks and two days.
And it falls short of the sun and the order of the stars by exactly five days in one period. And when this place that you see is completed [?].
Such is the appearance and likeness of all the light that Uriel, the great angel who is their leader, showed me.

In those days the angel Uriel answered me and said to me, “Look, Enoch, I have shown you everything and revealed everything to you, so that you may see this sun, this moon, those who lead the stars of heaven, and all those who bring them back—their workings, their seasons, and their appearances.”

And in the days of sinners, the rainy seasons will grow shorter, and their seed will be late on their land and in their fields. Everything produced on the earth will change and will not appear in its season; the rain will be withheld, and the sky will hold it back.
And at that time the fruit of the earth will be late and will not sprout in its season, and the fruit of the trees will be withheld in its season.
The moon will change its order and will not appear at its appointed time.
And in those days the sky will be seen, and drought will reach the edge of the great chariot in the west, and it will shine more brightly than the appointed measure of light.
And many leaders of the stars will stray from the command, and they will change their paths and their activities, and will not return at the times appointed for them.

And the entire order of the stars will be hidden from sinners, and the thoughts of those who live on the earth will go astray concerning them. They will turn away from all their paths, go astray, and regard them as gods.
And evil will increase upon them, and punishment will come upon them to destroy them all.
And he said to me, “Enoch, look at the book of the tablets of heaven, read what is written on them, and understand everything, one thing at a time.”

And I looked at everything on the tablets of heaven, read everything that was written, and understood it all. I read the book and everything written in it: all the deeds of humanity and all the children of flesh upon the earth, down to the generations of eternity.

And immediately afterward I blessed the great Lord, the eternal King of glory, because he had made all the works of the world. I praised the Lord for his patience, blessed him, and wept over the children of Adam.
And at that time I said, “Blessed is the person who dies righteous and good, against whom no record of wrongdoing has been written, and against whom no fault is found on the day of judgment.”

And those three holy ones brought me and set me on the earth before the door of my house. They said to me, “Make everything known to your son Methuselah, and show all your children that no flesh is righteous before the Lord, for he created them.

We will leave you with your children for one year, until you are commanded again, so that you may teach your children, write for them, and make all your children hear. And in the following year they will take you from among them.
Let your heart be strong, for the good will make righteousness known to the good. The righteous will rejoice with the righteous, and they will congratulate one another.
And sinner will die with sinner, and apostate will sink with apostate.
And those who practice righteousness will die because of the deeds of humanity, and will be gathered up because of the deeds of the wicked.”
And in those days they finished speaking with me, and I went to my people, blessing the Lord of the ages.

And now, my son Methuselah, I tell you all these things and write them down for you. I have revealed everything to you and given you the books containing all these things. My son Methuselah, preserve the books written by your father's hand, so that you may pass them on to future generations forever.

I have given wisdom to you, to your children, and to those who will be your descendants, so that they may pass this wisdom on to their children and to all generations forever, keeping it in their minds.
Those who understand will not sleep, but will listen with their ears so that they may learn this wisdom. It will please them more than fine food pleases those who eat it.

Blessed are all the righteous, and blessed are all those who walk in the path of righteousness and do not err like sinners in counting all their days, during which the sun travels in heaven, entering and leaving through the gates for thirty days, together with the leaders of thousands. This is the order of the stars, together with the four additional days that divide the four parts of the year. Their leaders guide them, and the four days enter with them.
Because of them people go astray and do not include them in the reckoning of the whole course of time, for people misunderstand them and do not know them accurately.

For they belong in the reckoning of the year and are truly assigned forever: one in the first gate, one in the third gate, one in the fourth gate, and one in the sixth gate. The year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.

The account is true, and its measured calculation is exact, for Uriel, the angel whom the Lord of all creation appointed for me, showed me the heavenly lights, the months, the festivals, the seasons, and the days, and breathed upon me through the power of heaven.
He has authority in heaven by day and by night to show light to human beings: the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the powers of heaven that revolve in their circles.
This is the order of the stars that set in their places, at their seasons, their festivals, and their months.
These are the names of those who lead them, who keep watch and enter at their appointed seasons, in their orders, at their times, in their months, under their authorities, and at their stations.

Their four leaders enter first, dividing the four parts of the year. After them come the twelve leaders of the orders, who divide the months, and the year's three hundred and sixty-four days, together with the leaders of thousands who distinguish the days and the four that are added to them. These leaders divide the four parts of the year.
These leaders of thousands stand between the leader and those who are led. One is added after each station, and their leaders make the divisions.
These are the names of the appointed leaders who divide the four parts of the year: Melkiel, Helommelek, Miliel, and Narel.

The names of those who lead them are Adnarel, Iyasusael, and Iylumiel. These three follow the leaders of the orders. One follows the three leaders of the orders, who follow those leaders of the stations who divide the four parts of the year.
At the beginning of the year, Melkiel rises first and rules. His name is called Tamaini and the Sun. All the days during which he rules under his authority are ninety-one days.

These are the signs of the days that appear on earth during the days of his authority: sweat, heat, and distress. All the trees bear fruit, leaves come out on all the trees, there is a wheat harvest, roses blossom, and all the flowers bloom in the open country, while the winter trees dry up.
These are the names of the leaders beneath them: Beraqiel and Zelebsael. The name of the other leader of a thousand who is added is Heluyaseph. The days of this one's authority are completed.
The other leader after them is Helommelek, whose name they call the Bright Sun. All the days of his authority are ninety-one days.

These are the signs of the days on earth: scorching heat and dryness. The trees bring forth their fruit, warmed and ripe, and yield their fruit dried. The ewes mate and become pregnant. All the produce of the earth and everything in the fields is gathered, and the grapes are pressed. This happens during the days of his authority.

These are their names, their orders, and their subordinate leaders, the leaders of thousands: Gidael, Keel, and Heel. The name of the leader of a thousand who is added with them is Asfael. The days of his authority are completed.
And now, my son Methuselah, I have shown you everything, and I will recount before you all the visions that I saw.

I saw two visions before I took a wife, and neither resembled the other. The first was when I was studying the book, and the second was before I married your mother. I saw a terrifying vision, and because of them I pleaded with the Lord.
While I was lying down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, I saw in a vision the sky being dashed apart and swept away and falling upon the earth.

As it fell upon the earth, I saw the earth being swallowed up in a great abyss. Mountains were suspended upon mountains, hills sank upon hills, and tall trees were cut off at their trunks, cast aside, and submerged in the abyss.
Then a word fell from it into my mouth, and I began to cry out and said, “The earth has been destroyed!”
Mahalalel, my grandfather, woke me while I was lying down and said to me, “Why are you crying out like this, my son, and why are you wailing like this?”

I told him the whole vision that I had seen, and he said to me, “You have seen something terrible, my son. Your dream vision is powerful, concerning the hidden things of all the sin of the earth. The earth is about to sink into the depths and suffer a great destruction.
“Now, my son, get up and plead with the Lord of glory, for you are faithful, so that a remnant may remain on the earth. He will wipe out the whole earth.
“My son, all this will come upon the earth from heaven, and there will be great destruction on the earth.”
From there I arose, prayed, and made supplication. I wrote down my prayer for the generations forever, and I have shown you everything, my son Methuselah.

When I went out below, I saw the sky, the sun rising in the east, the moon descending in the west, a few stars, the whole earth, and everything he had known before. I blessed the Lord of judgment and gave him glory, because he brought the sun out through the windows of the east, made it rise and shine across the face of heaven, and it rose and traveled the path shown to it.

I raised my hands in righteousness and blessed the Holy and Great One. I spoke with the breath of my mouth and with the tongue of flesh that God made for human beings so that they could speak with it. He gave them breath, a tongue, and a mouth so that they could speak with them.

“Blessed are you, Lord, King, great and mighty in your greatness, Lord of all the creatures of heaven, King of kings and God of the whole world. Your divinity, your kingship, and your greatness endure forever and ever, and your authority through every generation. All the heavens are your dwelling forever, and the whole earth is where your feet tread forever and ever.

“For you made everything, and you rule everything. No task is too difficult for you, not even one. No wisdom escapes you or turns away from the throne where you sit or from your presence. You know, see, and hear everything, and nothing is hidden from you, because you see everything.
“Now the angels of your heavens are doing wrong, and your wrath rests upon human flesh until the great day of judgment.

“Now, God and Lord and great King, I plead and ask that you grant my request: leave me descendants on the earth, and do not destroy all human flesh. Do not strip the earth bare, and do not let there be destruction forever.

“Now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh that has provoked your anger, but preserve righteous and upright flesh as a seed-bearing plant forever. Do not hide your face from the prayer of your servant, Lord.”
After this I saw another dream, and I will show you all of it, my son.
Enoch began speaking and said to his son Methuselah, “I am speaking to you, my son. Listen to my words and pay attention to your father’s dream vision.

“Before I married your mother Edna, I saw a vision on my bed. A bull came out of the earth, and that bull was white. After it, a female calf came out, and with her another calf came out. One of them was black and one was red.
“That black calf struck the red one and pursued it over the earth, and from then on I could not see that red calf.
“That black calf grew up, and a female calf came to be with it. I saw many cattle coming from it, resembling it and following behind it.
“That first female calf went away from the first bull and searched for the red calf, but did not find it. She wailed loudly for it and searched for it.
“I watched until that first bull came to her and quieted her, and from that time she no longer cried out.
“After this she gave birth to another white bull, and after it she gave birth to many cattle and black calves.
“In my sleep I saw that great white bull, and how it grew and became a great white bull. Many white cattle came from it, resembling it.
“They began giving birth to many white cattle that resembled them, and they followed one another.
“Again I looked with my eyes while I was sleeping, and I saw heaven above. A star fell from heaven, and it rose up, ate, and appeared among those cattle.
“After this I saw large black cattle. They all changed their pastures and their grazing places, and their calves [?], and they began to wail to one another.

“Again I saw in a vision and looked at heaven. I saw many stars descending and casting themselves down from heaven to that first star, among those calves. They became cattle with them and appeared among them.
“I looked at them, and they all exposed their genitals like horses and began mounting the heifers. All the heifers became pregnant and gave birth to elephants, camels, and donkeys.
“All the cattle feared them and were terrified of them. They began biting with their teeth, devouring, and goring with their horns.
Then they began to devour these bulls, and behold, all the children of the earth began to tremble and quake before them and to flee.
Again I saw them, and they began to strike one another and devour one another, and the earth began to cry out.
Again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw in a vision: behold, figures resembling white men came out of heaven. One came out of that place, and three were with them.

Those three who came out afterward took me by my hands, lifted me away from the offspring of the earth, and raised me to a high place. They showed me a tower high above the earth, and all the hills were lower.
They said to me, “Stay here until you see everything that will come upon these elephants, camels, and donkeys, and upon the stars and all the bulls.”

I saw one of those four who had come out first seize that first star which had fallen from heaven. He bound it hand and foot and threw it into an abyss. This abyss was narrow, deep, terrible, and dark.
One of them drew his sword and gave it to those elephants, camels, and donkeys. They began to strike one another, and the whole earth trembled because of them.

As I watched in the vision, behold, one of those four who had come out hurled stones from heaven. He gathered and took all the great stars whose genitals were like the genitals of horses, bound them all hand and foot, and threw them into a fissure in the earth.

One of those four went to that white bull and taught it a mystery while it trembled. That bull was born anew and became a man. He built himself a large boat and stayed in it. Three bulls stayed with him in that boat, and it was covered over them.
Again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw a high roof with seven channels upon it. These channels poured much water into one enclosure.

Again I saw, and behold, springs opened in the earth within that great enclosure. The water began to boil up and rise over the earth, concealing the enclosure until all its ground was covered with water.
Water, darkness, and mist increased over it, and I watched above that water. The water rose above that enclosure, poured over it, and stood upon the earth.
All the bulls in that enclosure gathered together, until I saw them sinking, being swallowed up, and perishing in that water.

That boat floated upon the water, while all the bulls, elephants, camels, and donkeys, and every animal, sank into the earth. I could not see them. They could not get out, but perished and sank into the deep.
Again I watched in the vision until those channels from that high roof stopped flowing, the fissure in the earth was leveled off, and other abysses were opened.
The water began to descend into them until the earth was uncovered. That boat rested on the earth, the darkness withdrew, and there was light.

That white bull which had become a man came out of that vessel, with three bulls beside him. One of those three bulls was white, resembling that bull; one of them was red like blood, and one was black. That white bull departed from them.

They began to produce wild animals and birds. From them came a mixture of all kinds: lions, leopards, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, pigs, falcons, eagles, vultures, kites, [?], and ravens. A white bull was born among them.
They began to bite one another. That white bull which had been born among them fathered a wild donkey and a white bull along with it, and the wild donkeys multiplied.
That bull which was born from him fathered a black wild boar and a white sheep. That wild boar fathered many pigs, and that sheep fathered twelve sheep.
When those twelve sheep had grown, they handed one of their number over to wild donkeys. Those wild donkeys, in turn, handed that sheep over to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.
The Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with him and graze with him among the wolves. They multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.

The wolves began to fear them and oppressed them until they destroyed their young. They threw their young into a stream of abundant water. Those sheep began to cry out because of their young and to complain to their Lord.

A sheep that had escaped from the wolves fled and went among the wild donkeys. I saw the sheep wailing and crying out, pleading with their Lord with all their strength, until that Lord of the sheep came down from his lofty palace at the sound of the sheep. He came to them and saw them.
He called that sheep which had escaped from the wolves and spoke to him about the wolves, telling him to warn them not to oppress the sheep.

That sheep went to the wolves at the Lord’s command. Another sheep met him and went with him. The two entered the assembly of those wolves together, spoke to them, and warned them not to oppress the sheep from that time onward.
After this I saw the wolves, and how they oppressed the sheep still more fiercely, with all their strength. The sheep cried out.
Their Lord came to the sheep and began to strike those wolves. The wolves began to wail, but the sheep became silent and from that time onward did not cry out.
I watched the sheep until they came out from among the wolves. The wolves’ eyes were darkened, and those wolves came out, pursuing the sheep with all their strength.
The Lord of the sheep went with them, leading them, and all his sheep followed him. His face was glorious and majestic, and his appearance was awe-inspiring and majestic.
The wolves began pursuing those sheep until they caught up with them at a body of water.
That body of water divided, and the water stood on either side before them. The Lord of the sheep led them and stood between them and the wolves.
Those wolves still did not see the sheep. The sheep went through the middle of that body of water, and the wolves followed the sheep. Those wolves ran after them through that body of water.

When they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee from his presence. That body of water came together and quickly returned to its original state. The water filled it and rose until it covered those wolves.
I watched until all the wolves that had followed those sheep were destroyed and drowned.

But the sheep crossed that water and went out into a wilderness where there was no water or grass. They began opening their eyes and seeing. I saw the Lord of the sheep tending them and giving them water and grass, while that sheep walked along, leading them.
He went up to the summit of that high rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent him to them.
From there I saw the Lord of the sheep standing before them. His appearance was great, awe-inspiring, and mighty. All those sheep saw him and were afraid of his presence.
All of them feared him and trembled, and they cried out after that sheep, to the other sheep who was with him and was among them: “We cannot stand before our Lord or look at him.”
That sheep who led them returned and went up to the summit of that rock. The sheep’s eyes began to darken, and they strayed from the path he had shown them, but that sheep did not know.

The Lord of the sheep became intensely angry with them. That sheep learned of it, came down from the summit of the rock, and went to the sheep. He found that most of them had darkened eyes and had strayed from his path.
When they saw him, they were afraid and trembled before him, and they wanted to return to their fold.

That sheep took other sheep with him, and they went to those sheep that had strayed and then killed them. The sheep were afraid of him. That sheep brought back those sheep that had strayed, and they returned to their folds.
In that vision I watched until that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep. He settled all the sheep in that house.

I watched until that sheep who had met the sheep that led the flock fell asleep. I watched until all the older sheep perished, and younger ones arose in their place. They entered a pasture and approached a river.
That sheep who led them and had become a man separated from them and fell asleep. All the sheep searched for him and cried out loudly over him.
I watched until they stopped crying over that sheep and crossed that flowing water. All the sheep who led them arose in place of those who had fallen asleep, and they led them.
I watched the sheep until they entered a good place, a pleasant and glorious land. I watched those sheep until they had eaten their fill, and that house was among them in the pleasant land.
Sometimes their eyes opened, and sometimes they darkened, until another sheep arose and led them. He brought them all back, and their eyes opened.
Dogs, foxes, and wild boars began devouring those sheep, until another sheep arose, one of their number, a ram who led them.
That ram began fighting on every side against those dogs, foxes, and wild boars, until he destroyed them all.
That sheep’s eyes were opened, and he saw that ram among the sheep, who had abandoned his glory and begun injuring those sheep. He trampled them and behaved disgracefully.
The Lord of the sheep sent the sheep to another sheep and raised him up to be a ram and lead the sheep in place of that sheep who had abandoned his glory.
And he went to him and spoke to him alone, and raised up that ram and made him ruler and leader of the sheep. Throughout all this, those dogs oppressed the sheep.
And the first ram drove away that second ram. That second ram rose and fled from his presence, and I watched until those dogs brought down the first ram.
That latter ram arose and led the young sheep. This latter ram fathered many sheep and lay down. A young sheep became a ram in his place and became ruler and leader of those sheep.

And those sheep grew and multiplied, and all those dogs, foxes, and wild boars were afraid and fled from him. That ram struck and killed all the wild animals, and those wild animals could no longer remain among the sheep, nor did they carry off anything at all from them.

And that house became large and spacious, and a tall tower was built for those sheep above that house for the Lord of the sheep. That house was low, but the tower rose up and was tall. The Lord of the sheep stood upon that tower, and they set a full table before him.

And again I saw those sheep stray again and go along many paths and abandon that house of theirs. The Lord of the sheep called some sheep from among them and sent them to the sheep, and the sheep began to kill them.

But one of them escaped and was not killed. He leaped away and cried out against the sheep, and they wanted to kill him. But the Lord of the sheep rescued him from the hands of the sheep, brought him up to me, and settled him there.
And he sent many other sheep to those sheep to make themselves heard and cry out against them.

And after that I saw when they abandoned the house of the Lord of the sheep and the tower, and strayed in every way, and their eyes became darkened. And I saw the Lord of the sheep bring great slaughter upon them in each of their pastures, until those sheep called for that slaughter and gave up his place.
He abandoned them into the hands of lions, leopards, wolves, and hyenas, into the hands of foxes, and to all the wild animals. Those wild animals began to tear those sheep apart.
And I saw that they abandoned that house of theirs and their tower. And he delivered them all into the hands of lions, to carry them off, and into the hands of all the wild animals, to devour them.
And I began to cry out with all my strength and call upon the Lord of the sheep, showing him what was happening to the sheep, because they were being eaten and swallowed by all the wild animals.
But he remained silent as he watched, and rejoiced because they were eaten, swallowed, and carried away. And he left them in the hands of all the wild animals to be eaten.

And he called seventy shepherds and entrusted those sheep to them to tend them. And he said to the shepherds and all their companions, “From now on, each one of you is to tend the sheep, and do everything that I command you.
“I will hand them over to you by number, and I will tell you which of them are to be destroyed; those you are to destroy.” And he handed those sheep over to them.
And he called another and said to him, “Pay attention and observe everything the shepherds do to these sheep, because they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.

“And write down every excess and destruction committed by the shepherds: how many they destroy at my command, and how many they destroy on their own. Write down all of it against each individual shepherd.

“And read out the numbers before me: how many they destroy and how many they hand over for destruction, so that this may be a testimony for me against them, and I may know everything the shepherds do. And I will hand them over and see what they do, whether they abide by the command I gave them or not.
“They must not know, and you must not show them or rebuke them. Rather, write down all the destruction caused by each individual shepherd, and bring it all up to me.”
And I watched until those shepherds tended the sheep, each in his own time. And they began to kill and destroy more than they had been commanded, and they left those sheep in the hands of lions.
And the lions ate and swallowed most of those sheep, and the leopards and wild boars ate with them. And they burned that tower and demolished that house of the sheep.
And I grieved very deeply over the tower, because that house of the sheep had been demolished. After that I could not see those sheep, whether they entered that house or did not enter it.

And the shepherds and their companions handed those sheep over to all the wild animals to eat them. And each one of them, in his own time, received them by number. And each one of them wrote for the other in a book how many he destroyed of them—for the other, in a book [?].
And each one killed and destroyed more than his prescribed number. And I began to weep and lament very deeply over those sheep.

In this way, in the vision, I saw the one who wrote, how he recorded each one destroyed by those shepherds every day. He went up, rested, and showed the entire book to the Lord of the sheep: everything they had done, everything each of them had destroyed, and everything they had handed over to destruction.
And the book was read before the Lord of the sheep. And he took the book in his hand, read it, sealed it, and put it away.

And after that I saw the shepherds tending the sheep for twelve hours. And behold, three of those sheep returned and came and entered, and began to rebuild everything that had fallen from that house. But the wild boars hindered them, and they could not.

And they began again to build as before, and they raised up that tower, and it was called the tall tower. And again I saw them set a table before the tower, but all the bread upon it was defiled and was not pure.

Besides all this, the eyes of these sheep were darkened, and they could not see; their shepherds were likewise blind. They were handed over to their shepherds for still greater destruction, and the shepherds trampled the sheep underfoot and devoured them.
The Lord of the sheep remained silent until all the sheep were scattered into the wilderness and mingled with them, and they did not rescue them from the power of the wild beasts.

The one who was writing the book brought it up, showed it, and read it at the dwellings of the Lord of the sheep. He pleaded with him on their behalf and petitioned him, showing him all the deeds of their shepherds and testifying before him against all the shepherds.
He took the book, placed it beside him, and went out.

I watched until the time when thirty-seven shepherds had tended them in this way. They all completed their respective periods, as the earlier ones had done. The sheep were handed over to others to tend them during their respective periods, each shepherd in his own period.

After this, I saw in a vision all the birds of the sky. Eagles, vultures, kites, and ravens came, and the eagles led all the birds. They began to devour those sheep, gouging out their eyes and eating their flesh.
The sheep cried out because their flesh was being eaten by the birds. I too cried out and lamented in my sleep against that shepherd who was tending the sheep.

I watched until the sheep were devoured by the dogs, the eagles, and the kites. They left them no intact flesh, no skin, and no sinew, until only their bones remained standing. Their bones too fell to the ground, and the sheep became few.
I watched until the time when twenty-three shepherds had tended them, and they completed their respective periods, fifty-eight periods in all.
Small white lambs were born to those sheep, and they began to open their eyes, to see, and to cry out to the sheep.
The sheep did not answer their cries or listen to what they told them. Instead, they became still more deaf, and their eyes became increasingly and severely darkened.
I saw in the vision that ravens flew down upon those lambs and seized one of them. They battered the sheep and devoured them.
I watched until horns grew on those lambs, but the ravens knocked their horns down. I watched until one great horn grew on one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.
It saw with them, and their eyes were opened. It cried out to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran toward it.
Despite all this, those eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites kept snatching the sheep, flying down upon them and devouring them. The sheep remained silent, but the rams lamented and cried out.
Those ravens struggled and fought with it. They wanted to tear out its horn, but they could not.

I watched them until the shepherds and eagles came, along with those eagles and kites. The ravens cried out for them to break the horn of that ram. They fought and battled with it, and it fought with them and cried out for help to come to it.

I watched until that man came who had written down the names of the shepherds and brought them up before the Lord of the sheep. He helped it and showed him everything, and his help came down to that ram.
I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath. All who saw him fled, and they all fell into darkness before his face.
All the eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites gathered together and brought with them all the sheep of the wilderness. They all came together and helped one another to break that ram's horn.

I watched that man who was writing the book at the Lord's command until he opened that book of the destruction caused by those last twelve shepherds. Before the Lord of the sheep, he showed that they had destroyed more than those before them.

I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them, took the rod of his wrath in his hand, and struck the earth. The earth split open, and all the birds of the sky and the wild beasts fell away from those sheep and sank into the earth, which closed over them.
I watched until a great sword was given to the sheep. The sheep went out against those wild beasts of the wilderness to kill them, and all the wild beasts and birds of the sky fled before them.
I watched until a throne was built in a pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat upon it. He took all the sealed books, and those books were opened before the Lord of the sheep.

The Lord summoned those first seven white ones and commanded them to bring before him, beginning with the first star that preceded them, those stars whose sexual organs were like the sexual organs of horses, and the first star that had fallen earlier. They brought them all before him.

He spoke to the man who was writing before him, who was one of the seven white ones, and said to him, “Take these seventy shepherds to whom I entrusted the sheep, and who took them and killed more of them than I commanded them to.”
And look, I saw them all bound, and they all stood before him.
Judgment came first upon the stars. They were judged and found guilty, and they went to the place of judgment. They threw them into an abyss filled with blazing fire and filled with pillars of fire.
Those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were thrown into this abyss of fire.

At that time I saw a similar abyss open in the middle of the earth, filled with fire. They brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty. They were thrown into this abyss of fire and burned. This abyss was to the right of that house.
I saw those sheep burning, and their bones were burning.

I stood watching until they folded up that old house and removed all its pillars. All the plants and the ornaments of that house were folded up with it. They took it out and put it in one place to the right of the land.

I watched the Lord of the sheep until he brought a new house, larger and higher than the first house, and set it in the place of the former one that had been rolled up. All its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and greater than those of the former old house that he had removed. All the sheep were inside it.
I saw all the sheep that remained, and all the animals on the earth and all the birds of the sky falling down and bowing to those sheep, pleading with them and obeying them in everything they said.

After that, those three who wore white and who had previously taken me up took me by the hand. With the hand of that ram also holding me, they took me up and set me among those sheep, before judgment took place.
Those sheep were all white, and their wool was thick and clean.

All those that had perished and been scattered, and all the wild animals and all the birds of the sky, gathered in that house. The Lord of the sheep rejoiced greatly because they had all become good and had returned to his house.

I watched until they laid down the sword that had been given to the sheep and brought it back into his house. It was sealed in the presence of the Lord. All the sheep were enclosed in that house, but it could not contain them.
The eyes of all of them were opened, and they saw clearly. There was not one among them who could not see.
I saw that the house was large and spacious and very full.
I saw a white bull born, and its horns were large. All the wild animals and the birds of the sky feared it and pleaded with it at all times.

I watched until all their kinds were transformed, and they all became white cattle. The first among them became [?], and that [?] became a large wild animal, with large black horns on its head. The Lord of the sheep rejoiced over them and over all the cattle.
I lay down among them, and I awoke and saw everything.
This was the vision that I saw while I slept. I awoke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave him glory.

After that I wept bitterly, and my tears did not stop, until I could no longer endure it, as I saw what would come down upon what I had seen. For everything would come to pass and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of humanity, each in its part, were shown to me.
That night I remembered my first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled, for I had seen that vision.

“And now, my son Methuselah, call all your brothers to me and gather all your mother’s children to me. For a voice calls me, and a spirit has been poured out upon me, so that I may show you everything that will happen to you forever.”
Then Methuselah went and called all his brothers to him and gathered his relatives.

He spoke about righteousness to all his children and said, “Listen, my children, to everything your father says, and pay close attention to the words of my mouth. For I will make you hear and tell you, my beloved: love uprightness and walk in it.”

“Do not approach uprightness with a divided heart, and do not associate with those who have divided hearts. Instead, walk in righteousness, my children, and it will lead you along good paths, and righteousness will be your companion.”

For I know that violence will become firmly established on the earth, and a great scourge will come upon the earth. All injustice will come to an end and be cut off at its roots, and every structure will pass away.
And injustice will return again and run its course on the earth, and every act of injustice, violence, and sin will be taken up again.

And when injustice, sin, blasphemy, violence, and every deed increase, and rebellion, sin, and uncleanness increase, a great scourge will come from heaven upon all these. The holy Lord will come forth with wrath and a great scourge to execute judgment upon the earth.
In those days violence will be cut off at its roots, and the roots of injustice, together with deceit, will be destroyed from beneath heaven.

Everything will be handed over along with the nations, and the storehouse will burn with fire. They will drive them out of the whole earth, and they will be thrown into the judgment of fire and destroyed in wrath and in a mighty judgment that lasts forever.
The righteous will rise from sleep, and wisdom will arise and be given to them.

Then the roots of injustice will be cut off, and sinners will be destroyed by the sword. They will be cut off from the blasphemers in every place, and those who devise violence and practice blasphemy will be destroyed by slaughter.

After this there will be another week, the eighth, a week of righteousness. A sword will be given to it so that righteous judgment may be executed upon those who commit violence, and sinners will be handed over to the righteous.
At its end they will acquire houses through their righteousness, and a house will be built for the great King in glory forever.

After this, in the ninth week, righteous judgment will be revealed to the whole world. All the deeds of the wicked will depart from the earth, and the world will be recorded for destruction, and all people will look toward the path of uprightness.
After this, in the tenth week, in its seventh part, there will be eternal judgment, and it will be carried out against the Watchers, and a great eternal heaven that springs up among the angels [?].
The first heaven will depart and pass away, and a new heaven will appear, and all the powers of the heavens will shine seven times more brightly forever.
After this there will be many weeks, beyond counting, forever in goodness and righteousness. From then on, sin will never again be spoken of.
And now I tell you, my children, and show you the paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. I will show you again so that you may know what is coming.
And now listen to me, my children, and walk in the paths of righteousness. Do not walk in the paths of violence, for all who walk in the path of injustice will be destroyed forever.

What was written by Enoch. Enoch, praised by all people and ruler of the whole earth, wrote all this instruction in wisdom for all my children who dwell on earth and for the later generations who practice uprightness and peace.
Do not let your spirits grieve over the times, for the Holy and Great One has given days to everyone.
The righteous will rise from sleep; he will rise and proceed along the path of righteousness. His entire path and his journey will be in goodness and everlasting mercy.
He will show mercy to the righteous and give him everlasting uprightness. He will give him authority, and he will live in goodness and righteousness and walk in everlasting light.
Sin will be destroyed in darkness forever, and from that day onward it will never again be seen.
After this, Enoch was present and began to speak from the books.

Enoch said, “Concerning the children of righteousness, the chosen ones of the world, and the plant of righteousness and uprightness, I tell you these things and make them known to you, my children. I am Enoch, to whom these things were shown in a heavenly vision. I learned them from the words of the holy angels, and I understood them from the tablets of heaven.”
Then Enoch began to speak from the books and said, “I was born seventh in the first week, while righteous judgment still endured.

After me, in the second week, great evil will arise, and deceit will spring up. In it the first end will occur, and in it a man will be saved. After it has ended, injustice will increase, and he will establish a law for sinners.
After this, at the end of the third week, a man will be chosen as the plant of righteous judgment, and after him the plant of righteousness and uprightness will come forth forever.
After this, at the end of the fourth week, visions of the holy and righteous will appear, and a law for generation after generation and an enclosure will be made for them.
After this, at the end of the fifth week, a house of glory and kingship will be built forever.

After this, in the sixth week, all who live in it will be blinded, and all their hearts will forget wisdom. In it a man will ascend, and at its end the royal house will be burned with fire. In it the entire family of the chosen root will be scattered.
After this, in the seventh week, a rebellious generation will arise. Its deeds will be many, and all its deeds will be rebellion.
At its completion, the chosen righteous ones from the eternal plant of righteousness will be rewarded. They will be given sevenfold instruction concerning all his creation.
For who among human beings can hear the voice of the Holy One without being shaken? Who can think his thoughts? And who can look upon heaven and all its works?

And what is it that can know the workings of heaven? And how can he see his soul, unless it is his spirit? Can he tell of it without having ascended, or see all their wings and contemplate them without acting as they do?
And who among all human beings can know the breadth and length of the earth? And to whom has the full extent of all these things been shown?
And how can there be any human being who can know the extent of heaven—that is, its height—and what it rests upon, how many stars there are, and where all the heavenly lights rest?
And now I tell you, my children: Love righteousness and walk in it, for the paths of righteousness deserve to be accepted, but the paths of injustice will quickly perish and diminish.
The paths of violence and death will be revealed to people known from their birth, and they will keep far from them and not follow them.
And now I tell you who are righteous: Do not walk in the paths of evil and violence, or in the paths of death. Do not approach them, so that you will not perish.
Instead, desire and choose for yourselves righteousness and a chosen life, and walk in the paths of peace, so that you may live and prosper.

Hold fast to this in the thoughts of your hearts, and do not let my words be erased from your hearts. For I know that sinners will counsel people to practice evil wisdom, but no place will be found for it, and no suffering will diminish.
Woe to those who build injustice and violence and lay the foundations of robbery, for they will quickly be uprooted and will have no peace.

Woe to those who build their houses through sin, for they will be uprooted from all their foundations and will fall by the sword. Those who acquire gold and silver will quickly be destroyed in judgment.
Woe to you who are rich, for you have trusted in your wealth. You will be deprived of your wealth, because you did not remember the Most High in the days of your wealth.
You have committed blasphemy and injustice, and you have made yourselves ready for the day of bloodshed, the day of darkness, and the day of great judgment.
This is what I say, and I make it known to you: The one who created you will overthrow you, and there will be no mercy when you fall. Your Creator will rejoice in your destruction.
In those days, the righteous among you will be a reproach to sinners and the wicked.
Who will grant that my eyes become clouds of heaven, so that I may weep over you and pour out my tears like a rain cloud, and find relief from the sorrow of my heart?
Who allowed you to practice hatred and evil? And judgment will overtake you sinners.
Do not fear sinners, you righteous people, for God will again deliver them into your hands, so that you may pass judgment on them as you wish.
Woe to you who pronounce curses that cannot be undone! Healing is far from you because of your sins.
Woe to you who repay your neighbors with evil, for you will be repaid according to your deeds.
Woe to you who bear false witness and prepare injustice, for you will quickly perish.
Woe to you sinners, for you persecute the righteous! You yourselves will be turned back and driven away because of injustice, and their yoke will weigh heavily upon you.
Have hope, you righteous people, for sinners will quickly perish before you, and you will have authority over them as you wish.

On the day of the sinners’ distress, your young will rise and be lifted up like eagles, and your shelter will be greater than that of kites. You will ascend and enter the clefts of the earth and the crevices of the rocks forever, like a hyrax fleeing from the unjust, and they will groan over you.

You will not be like them, but this will be a witness against you: that you became companions of sinners. They will weep like sirens. But you who have suffered, do not fear, for healing will be yours, a bright light will shine upon you, and you will hear a voice of rest from heaven.
Woe to you sinners, for your wealth makes you appear righteous, but your hearts accuse you of being sinners. This matter will be a witness against you, a reminder of your evil deeds.
Woe to you who eat the richness of wheat and drink the strength of the root of the spring [?], and drive sinners away by your power.
Woe to you who drink water at all times, for you will soon be repaid, brought to an end, and dried up, because you have abandoned the spring of life.
Woe to you who commit injustice, theft, and slander! This will be remembered against you for evil.
Woe to you sinners who oppress the righteous by force, for the day of your destruction is coming. In those days, many good days will come to the righteous, on the day of your judgment.
Have confidence, you righteous, for sinners will be put to shame and destroyed on the day of injustice.
Let it be known to you that the Most High will remember your destruction, and the angels will rejoice over your destruction.
What will you do, you sinners, and where will you flee on that day of judgment, when you hear the sound of the prayers of the righteous?
Do not be like them. Rather, this statement will be a witness against them: “You have become partners with sinners.”
In those days the prayers of the holy ones will reach the Lord, and the days of your judgment will come upon you.
Every account of their injustice will be recited before the Great and Holy One. Your faces will be put to shame, and every deed established through injustice will be rejected.
Woe to you sinners who are in the midst of the sea and on dry land, whose remembrance brings evil upon you!
